items.use: Tell a friend, staff or the police box (kouban) that your wallet is gone.

example.romaji: yabai, saifu nakushita kamo. doko da?
example.ja: やばい、財布なくしたかも。どこだ？
example.english: Oh no, I think I lost my wallet. Where is it?

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, saifu o nakushite shimatta n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、財布をなくしてしまったんですが。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, I've lost my wallet.

items.notes: nakusu is 'lose'; otoshita (dropped it) is just as common.

blocks.label: Mistakes and running late
blocks.rationale: Own up to a slip or say you'll be late.
blocks.interference: machigaechatta is your own mistake; machigatteru says something is wrong.

items.english: oops, I got it wrong; I made a mistake
items.use: Admit a slip like a wrong number, train or answer; the -chatta adds an 'oops'.

example.romaji: a, densha machigaechatta. tsugi de oriyou.
example.ja: あ、電車間違えちゃった。次で降りよう。
example.english: Oh, I got on the wrong train. Let's get off at the next stop.

examplePolite.romaji: a, densha o machigaete shimaimashita. tsugi de orimasu.
examplePolite.ja: あ、電車を間違えてしまいました。次で降ります。
examplePolite.english: Oh, I took the wrong train. I'll get off at the next stop.

items.notes: machigaeru is 'get something wrong'; machigatteru is 'it's wrong'.

items.english: I won't make it in time; there's not enough time
items.use: Panic about a train or deadline; ma ni atta is 'made it!'

example.romaji: yabai, kono mama ja ma ni awanai!
example.ja: やばい、このままじゃ間に合わない！
example.english: Oh no, at this rate I won't make it!

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, kono mama da to ma ni aimasen.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、このままだと間に合いません。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, at this rate I won't make it in time.

items.notes: ma ni atte imasu also politely declines: 'I'm fine, thanks, I have enough'.

items.english: this is a problem; what do I do now?
items.use: Muttered when you're stuck; someone nearby may offer help: dou shita n desu ka? (what's wrong?).

example.romaji: komatta na, kagi ga mitsukaranai.
example.ja: 困ったな、鍵が見つからない。
example.english: This is a problem, I can't find my keys.

examplePolite.romaji: komarimashita ne, kagi ga mitsukarimasen.
examplePolite.ja: 困りましたね、鍵が見つかりません。
examplePolite.english: This is a problem. I can't find my keys.

items.notes: Staff offer help with nanika okomari desu ka? (is something wrong?).

items.use: The standard excuse for being late in the morning.

example.romaji: gomen, nebou shita! juppun okureru.
example.ja: ごめん、寝坊した！十分遅れる。
example.english: Sorry, I overslept! I'll be ten minutes late.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, nebou shimashita. juppun hodo okuremasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、寝坊しました。十分ほど遅れます。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I overslept. I'll be about ten minutes late.

blocks.label: At your limit
blocks.rationale: Say you can't take any more.
blocks.interference: mou dame, mou muri and mou genkai overlap; mou muri is the most casual.

items.english: I can't go on; it's hopeless; I'm done for
items.use: Said when you're exhausted, overwhelmed or think it's all over.

example.romaji: mou dame, ashi ga ugokanai.
example.ja: もうダメ、足が動かない。
example.english: I can't go on, my legs won't move.

items.notes: dame alone is 'no good' or 'not allowed'; mou adds 'any more'.

items.use: Give up on food, work or a situation; young people say it about small things too.

example.romaji: mou muri, kore ijou taberarenai.
example.ja: もう無理、これ以上食べられない。
example.english: I can't, I can't eat any more.

items.notes: muri is 'impossible'; muri shinaide is 'don't push yourself'.

items.use: Said when tiredness, stress or patience has run out; heavier than mou muri.

example.romaji: nemukute mou genkai. saki ni neru ne.
example.ja: 眠くてもう限界。先に寝るね。
example.english: I'm too sleepy to keep going. I'm heading to bed.

examplePolite.romaji: nemukute mou genkai desu. saki ni yasumimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 眠くてもう限界です。先に休みます。
examplePolite.english: I'm too sleepy to go on. I'll turn in first.

items.notes: genkai is 'limit'; you'll hear it about overtime and deadlines too.

blocks.label: Nerves and relief
blocks.rationale: Say you're nervous, then relieved or feeling better.
blocks.interference: anshin shita and hotto shita are near twins; kinchou isn't excitement.

items.use: Before an interview, a speech or meeting someone important; kinchou shiteru is 'I'm nervous right now'.

example.romaji: ashita mensetsu da kara, sugoku kinchou suru.
example.ja: 明日面接だから、すごく緊張する。
example.english: I've got an interview tomorrow, so I'm really nervous.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita mensetsu na node, totemo kinchou shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日面接なので、とても緊張します。
examplePolite.english: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'm very nervous.

items.notes: Not 'excited': wakuwaku suru is the happy kind of nerves.

items.english: what a relief; I feel reassured
items.use: When news or someone's words remove a worry; tell others anshin shite (don't worry).

example.romaji: kekka, daijoubu datta. anshin shita.
example.ja: 結果、大丈夫だった。安心した。
example.english: The results were fine. What a relief.

examplePolite.romaji: kekka ga daijoubu de, anshin shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 結果が大丈夫で、安心しました。
examplePolite.english: I'm relieved the results were fine.

items.notes: The opposite is shinpai (worry).

items.use: The sigh when a worry ends: a test passed, someone arrived safe.

example.romaji: buji de yokatta. hotto shita yo.
example.ja: 無事でよかった。ほっとしたよ。
example.english: I'm so glad you're safe. What a relief.

examplePolite.romaji: buji de yokatta desu. hotto shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 無事でよかったです。ほっとしました。
examplePolite.english: I'm glad you're safe. What a relief.

items.notes: Close to anshin shita; hotto shita is the instant release, anshin the calm that follows.

items.english: I feel better; it got easier
items.use: After medicine, rest or a weight off your mind; also when a task gets easier.

example.romaji: kusuri nondara, daibu raku ni natta.
example.ja: 薬飲んだら、だいぶ楽になった。
example.english: After the medicine, I feel a lot better.

examplePolite.romaji: kusuri o nondara, daibu raku ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 薬を飲んだら、だいぶ楽になりました。
examplePolite.english: I took the medicine and feel much better.

items.notes: raku is 'ease': raku ni shite kudasai is 'make yourself comfortable'.

blocks.label: Formal apologies
blocks.rationale: Lets you apologize properly at work or to customers.
blocks.interference: Gozaimasen is staff-level formal; arimasen is enough for you.

items.use: A serious apology at work or to customers, for a mistake or an inconvenience.
items.kana: もうしわけありません

example.romaji: hontou ni moushiwake arimasen. sugu ni naoshimasu.
example.ja: 本当に申し訳ありません。すぐに直します。
example.english: I'm truly sorry. I'll fix it right away.

items.notes: Stronger than sumimasen; the right level for your own work mistakes.

items.use: Staff to customers, and in official apologies and announcements.
items.kana: もうしわけございません

example.romaji: omatase shite, moushiwake gozaimasen.
example.ja: お待たせして、申し訳ございません。
example.english: We're very sorry to keep you waiting.

items.notes: You'll hear it far more than you say it; moushiwake arimasen is enough for you.

items.english: sorry to bother you when you're busy
items.use: Opens a request or question to a coworker, a clerk or a teacher.
items.ja: お忙しいところすみません
items.kana: おいそがしいところすみません

example.romaji: oisogashii tokoro sumimasen, chotto ii desu ka?
example.ja: お忙しいところすみません、ちょっといいですか？
example.english: Sorry to bother you, do you have a moment?

items.notes: A set opener; say it even if they don't look busy.

items.english: sorry for the trouble I caused
items.use: Apology to coworkers or neighbours after you caused them trouble: a sick day, a mistake, noise.
items.ja: ご迷惑をおかけしました
items.kana: ごめいわくをおかけしました

example.romaji: kinou wa yasunde shimatte, gomeiwaku o okake shimashita.
example.ja: 昨日は休んでしまって、ご迷惑をおかけしました。
example.english: Sorry for the trouble my day off caused yesterday.

items.notes: Meiwaku is trouble or nuisance. Casual: meiwaku kakete gomen.

blocks.label: Rough and pleading apologies
blocks.rationale: Lets you catch blunt or desperate apologies in casual talk and drama.
blocks.interference: Suman is masculine and casual; never use it upward.

items.use: Quick apology from men to friends or juniors; also a gruff thanks.

example.romaji: suman, okureta. densha ga tomatteta.
example.ja: すまん、遅れた。電車が止まってた。
example.english: Sorry I'm late. The train had stopped.

items.notes: Never to a superior. Sumanai is an older, stiffer version.

items.use: Plain-form apology, often from men or older people to friends, family or juniors.

example.romaji: isogashii no ni, moushiwake nai na.
example.ja: 忙しいのに、申し訳ないな。
example.english: Sorry to put you out when you're busy.

examplePolite.romaji: oisogashii no ni, moushiwake arimasen.
examplePolite.ja: お忙しいのに、申し訳ありません。
examplePolite.english: I'm sorry to trouble you when you're busy.

items.notes: Also 'I feel bad': kare ni moushiwake nai (I feel bad toward him).

items.use: Pleading with someone close after hurting them, or a playful 'go easy on me'.

example.romaji: hontou ni gomen. onegai, yurushite.
example.ja: 本当にごめん。お願い、許して。
example.english: I'm really sorry. Please forgive me.

examplePolite.romaji: hontou ni sumimasen deshita. douka yurushite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 本当にすみませんでした。どうか許してください。
examplePolite.english: I'm truly sorry. Please forgive me.

items.notes: Heavy for everyday slips, where gomen is enough.

blocks.label: Work replies
blocks.rationale: Lets you answer requests and instructions politely at work or with staff.
blocks.interference: Kentou shimasu usually means no; shouchi shimashita is a firm yes.

items.use: Said when you need to look something up or ask someone before answering; staff say it a lot.

example.romaji: sumimasen, chotto kakunin shimasu ne.
example.ja: すみません、ちょっと確認しますね。
example.english: Sorry, let me just check.

items.notes: Casual: chotto mite miru. Staff often say kakunin itashimasu.

items.use: A polite yes to an instruction or request at work or from a customer.

example.romaji: shouchi shimashita. ashita made ni okurimasu.
example.ja: 承知しました。明日までに送ります。
example.english: Understood. I'll send it by tomorrow.

items.notes: Wakarimashita is fine with coworkers; kashikomarimashita is the shop-staff version.

items.use: Humble version of onegai shimasu for requests at work, on the phone and from staff.

example.romaji: kochira no shorui, yoroshiku onegai itashimasu.
example.ja: こちらの書類、よろしくお願いいたします。
example.english: Please take care of these documents.

items.notes: Onegai shimasu is enough in daily life.

items.english: I'll think it over; we'll consider it
items.use: A business reply to a proposal or sales pitch; often a soft no.

example.romaji: sou desu ne, chotto kentou shimasu.
example.ja: そうですね、ちょっと検討します。
example.english: Hmm, let me think it over.

items.notes: Don't read it as a yes; a real yes sounds like zehi or onegai shimasu.

items.use: Staff and business people use it for thanks or before asking a favour; you'll mostly hear it.

example.romaji: osoreirimasu ga, onamae o ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: 恐れ入りますが、お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか？
example.english: Excuse me, may I ask your name?

items.notes: Osoreirimasu ga at the start works like a very polite sumimasen ga.

blocks.label: Modest replies
blocks.rationale: Lets you answer praise and kind questions modestly.
blocks.interference: Mada mada desu is about yourself; mada mada da na said to someone else is a put-down.

items.english: I'm well, thank you; thanks to you
items.use: Polite answer when asked how you or your family are, or when congratulated.

example.romaji: okagesama de, kodomo mo genki desu.
example.ja: おかげさまで、子供も元気です。
example.english: We're well, thank you. The kids are fine too.

items.notes: Thanks for general goodwill, not for something they actually did.

items.english: I've still got a long way to go
items.use: Modest reply to praise, especially of your Japanese; start with iie.

example.romaji: iie, nihongo wa mada mada desu.
example.ja: いいえ、日本語はまだまだです。
example.english: Oh no, my Japanese has a long way to go.

items.notes: Casual: mada mada da yo.

items.use: The humble reply to a compliment (iie, mada mada desu), or says something is far from good enough; said about someone else it's a put-down.

example.romaji: shiai ni katta kedo, mada mada da na.
example.ja: 試合に勝ったけど、まだまだだな。
example.english: We won the match, but we've still got a long way to go.

examplePolite.romaji: shiai ni wa kachimashita ga, mada mada desu.
examplePolite.ja: 試合には勝ちましたが、まだまだです。
examplePolite.english: We won the match, but we've still got a long way to go.

items.notes: Also 'still lots more': mada mada aru (there's plenty left).

items.use: Humble way to talk about your own help, usually in oyaku ni tatete ureshii (glad I could help).

example.romaji: oyaku ni tatete yokatta. mata itsu demo itte ne.
example.ja: お役に立ててよかった。またいつでも言ってね。
example.english: Glad I could help. Ask me anytime.

examplePolite.romaji: oyaku ni tatete ureshii desu. mata itsu demo douzo.
examplePolite.ja: お役に立ててうれしいです。またいつでもどうぞ。
examplePolite.english: I'm glad I could help. Feel free to ask anytime.

items.notes: Plain yaku ni tatsu means 'be useful': kono apuri, yaku ni tatsu yo.

blocks.label: Office set phrases
blocks.rationale: Lets you handle the fixed greetings of work calls, emails and coming back to the office.
blocks.interference: Tadaima modorimashita is for the office; at home it's just tadaima.

items.english: thanks for your continued support (business greeting)
items.use: Opens almost every work phone call or email to a client or partner; the other side answers kochira koso osewa ni natte orimasu.
items.ja: お世話になっております
items.kana: おせわになっております

example.romaji: itsumo osewa ni natte orimasu. tanaka desu.
example.ja: いつもお世話になっております。田中です。
example.english: Hello, it's Tanaka. Thanks as always for your support.

items.notes: The past form osewa ni narimashita thanks someone who looked after you, e.g. when you leave a host family or a job.

items.use: Said on walking back into the office after going out; colleagues answer okaerinasai or otsukaresama desu.
items.kana: ただいまもどりました

example.romaji: tadaima modorimashita. nanika arimashita ka?
example.ja: ただいま戻りました。何かありましたか？
example.english: I'm back. Did anything come up?

items.notes: At home just say tadaima.

items.use: Polite lead-in before asking a client, staff member or stranger to do something; common in business emails, on forms and in announcements.

example.romaji: otesuu desu ga, kochira ni onamae o onegai shimasu.
example.ja: お手数ですが、こちらにお名前をお願いします。
example.english: Sorry to trouble you, but could you write your name here?

items.notes: Otesuu o okake shimasu means sorry for the trouble I'm causing. With friends say warui kedo instead.

blocks.label: Counting on someone
blocks.rationale: Lets you lean on someone, plead with them, and promise to deliver.
blocks.interference: Tanomu yo asks for help; tanomu kara begs someone to stop or act.

items.use: Said with confidence when you take on a job someone is worried about.

example.romaji: ryouri? makasete! tokui da kara.
example.ja: 料理？任せて！得意だから。
example.english: Cooking? Leave it to me, I'm good at it.

examplePolite.romaji: sono ken wa watashi ni makasete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: その件は私に任せてください。
examplePolite.english: Please leave that to me.

items.notes: Makaseru means to entrust. Omakase at a sushi bar means chef's choice.

items.use: Presses a request on a friend or junior, or tells them you're relying on them; the answer is makasete.

example.romaji: ashita no junbi, tanomu yo.
example.ja: 明日の準備、頼むよ。
example.english: I'm counting on you to get things ready for tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita no junbi, onegai shimasu ne.
examplePolite.ja: 明日の準備、お願いしますね。
examplePolite.english: I'll leave tomorrow's prep to you, then.

items.notes: Women usually say onegai ne instead.

items.use: Desperate or exasperated plea to a friend or family member to stop or do something.

example.romaji: tanomu kara, mou yamete.
example.ja: 頼むから、もうやめて。
example.english: Please, I'm begging you, just stop.

items.notes: Stronger than tanomu yo. Onegai dakara is the softer version anyone can use.

items.use: Emotional plea, usually before stop, listen or don't go.

example.romaji: onegai dakara, hanashi kiite.
example.ja: お願いだから、話聞いて。
example.english: Please, just listen to me.

examplePolite.romaji: onegai desu kara, yamete kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: お願いですから、やめてください。
examplePolite.english: Please, I'm begging you, stop.

items.notes: Softer than tanomu kara and used by everyone.

blocks.label: Meals at home
blocks.rationale: Lets you call people to the table, serve them and offer seconds.
blocks.interference: Meshiagare is said by the cook; the eater says itadakimasu.

items.use: Asks for another bowl of rice or a refill, or offers one (okawari wa?).

example.romaji: okawari aru yo. iru?
example.ja: おかわりあるよ。いる？
example.english: There's seconds. Want some?

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, gohan no okawari onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、ご飯のおかわりお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, could I get more rice?

items.notes: Okawari jiyuu means free refills. As a verb: okawari suru.

items.use: Said by the cook at home as they serve, usually douzo meshiagare, often in reply to itadakimasu.
items.politeJa: 召し上がってください

example.romaji: hai, dekita yo. douzo meshiagare.
example.ja: はい、できたよ。どうぞ召し上がれ。
example.english: Okay, it's ready. Dig in.

examplePolite.romaji: douzo, meshiagatte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: どうぞ、召し上がってください。
examplePolite.english: Please, go ahead and eat.

items.notes: Homey and a little playful; staff and formal hosts say meshiagatte kudasai instead.

items.use: Called out at home, usually by a parent, to get everyone to the table.

example.romaji: minna, gohan da yo! hayaku kite.
example.ja: みんな、ご飯だよ！早く来て。
example.english: Everyone, food's ready! Come quick.

examplePolite.romaji: gohan desu yo. douzo suwatte kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: ご飯ですよ。どうぞ座ってください。
examplePolite.english: The meal's ready. Please sit down.

items.notes: Gohan means a meal as well as cooked rice.

items.use: Urges someone to start eating or drinking now; usually followed by douzo or tabete.
items.politeJa: 冷めないうちにどうぞ

example.romaji: hora, samenai uchi ni tabete.
example.ja: ほら、冷めないうちに食べて。
example.english: Come on, eat it while it's hot.

examplePolite.romaji: samenai uchi ni douzo.
examplePolite.ja: 冷めないうちにどうぞ。
examplePolite.english: Please, have it before it gets cold.

items.notes: -nai uchi ni means before something happens: kuraku naranai uchi ni (before it gets dark).

blocks.label: Clinic and front desk
blocks.rationale: Lets you follow reception at a clinic, office or business phone line.
blocks.interference: Ukagau means ask here, but come or visit in tadaima ukagaimasu.

items.english: what brings you in today?; what seems to be the problem?
items.use: The doctor's opening question; answer with your symptom, like nodo ga itai n desu (my throat hurts).
items.ja: 今日はどうされましたか
items.kana: きょうはどうされましたか

example.romaji: konnichiwa. kyou wa dou saremashita ka?
example.ja: こんにちは。今日はどうされましたか？
example.english: Hello. What brings you in today?

items.notes: Dou shita no? is what a friend would ask: what's wrong?

items.use: How shops and companies answer the phone, followed by their name; reply with your name and what you want.
items.ja: お電話ありがとうございます
items.kana: おでんわありがとうございます

example.romaji: odenwa arigatou gozaimasu. sakura shokudou desu.
example.ja: お電話ありがとうございます。さくら食堂です。
example.english: Thank you for calling. This is Sakura Diner.

items.notes: Not used on personal calls, where people answer with moshimoshi.

items.use: Clinic or pharmacy reception asks for it when you check in; hand over the card.
items.ja: 保険証をお願いします
items.kana: ほけんしょうをおねがいします

example.romaji: hajimete desu ka? hokenshou o onegai shimasu.
example.ja: 初めてですか？保険証をお願いします。
example.english: Is this your first visit? Your insurance card, please.

items.notes: Many clinics now take the My Number card instead: mainanbaa kaado.

items.romaji: onamae o ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka
items.use: Reception, phone staff or a booking desk asks it; answer with your family name + desu.
items.ja: お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか
items.kana: おなまえをうかがってもよろしいですか

example.romaji: kakunin shimasu node, onamae o ukagatte mo yoroshii desu ka?
example.ja: 確認しますので、お名前を伺ってもよろしいですか？
example.english: May I have your name so I can check?

items.notes: Ukagau here is the humble verb for ask; a friend would just say namae wa?

blocks.label: Calling back
blocks.rationale: Lets you put off a call and follow up on one you missed.
blocks.interference: Denwa suru (call) versus kakenaosu and orikaesu (call back).

items.use: Said to friends or family when you can't talk now or want to talk later, often with ne.

example.romaji: ima isogashii kara, ato de denwa suru ne.
example.ja: 今忙しいから、後で電話するね。
example.english: I'm busy now, so I'll call you later.

examplePolite.romaji: kaigi no ato de denwa shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 会議の後で電話します。
examplePolite.english: I'll call you after the meeting.

items.notes: To a client or senior, ato de odenwa shimasu is the humble version.

items.use: Said when you can't talk right now; usually with ne.

example.romaji: gomen, ima densha. ato de kakenaosu ne.
example.ja: ごめん、今電車。後でかけ直すね。
example.english: Sorry, I'm on the train. I'll call you back later.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, ima te ga hanasenai node, ato de kakenaoshimasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、今手が離せないので、後でかけ直します。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I'm tied up right now, so I'll call you back later.

items.notes: Kakenaosu means call again; kakeru alone means make a call.

items.english: I'll call you back; we'll return your call
items.use: Business phrase: staff say it when the person you want is out, and you can use it at work too.
items.ja: 折り返しお電話します
items.kana: おりかえしおでんわします

example.romaji: tantousha ga modorimashitara, orikaeshi odenwa shimasu.
example.ja: 担当者が戻りましたら、折り返しお電話します。
example.english: When the person in charge is back, we'll call you back.

items.notes: Casual: orikaesu ne. Orikaeshi denwa kudasai means please call me back.

items.use: Said or texted when you call back after missing someone's call.
items.ja: 電話出られなくてごめん
items.kana: でんわでられなくてごめん
items.politeJa: お電話に出られずすみませんでした

example.romaji: denwa derarenakute gomen. dou shita no?
example.ja: 電話出られなくてごめん。どうしたの？
example.english: Sorry I missed your call. What's up?

examplePolite.romaji: sakki wa odenwa ni derarezu sumimasen deshita.
examplePolite.ja: さっきはお電話に出られずすみませんでした。
examplePolite.english: Sorry I couldn't take your call earlier.

items.notes: Denwa ni deru means answer the phone; casual speech drops the ni.

blocks.label: Year-end and New Year
blocks.rationale: Greet people around Christmas and New Year.
blocks.interference: yoi otoshi o is before January 1, akemashite omedetou after.

items.use: Said from January 1 into early January, the first time you see someone; never before New Year.
items.ja: あけましておめでとう
items.kana: あけましておめでとう
items.politeJa: あけましておめでとうございます

example.romaji: akemashite omedetou! kotoshi mo yoroshiku ne.
example.ja: あけましておめでとう！今年もよろしくね。
example.english: Happy New Year! Here's to another year.

examplePolite.romaji: akemashite omedetou gozaimasu. kotoshi mo yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: あけましておめでとうございます。今年もよろしくお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Happy New Year. I look forward to another year with you.

items.notes: Friends shorten it to akeome.

items.use: Said among friends and couples; in Japan Christmas Eve is a date night, not a family holiday.

example.romaji: merii kurisumasu! kore, purezento da yo.
example.ja: メリークリスマス！これ、プレゼントだよ。
example.english: Merry Christmas! Here's your present.

examplePolite.romaji: merii kurisumasu. kore, purezento desu.
examplePolite.ja: メリークリスマス。これ、プレゼントです。
examplePolite.english: Merry Christmas. This is a present for you.

items.notes: Friends shorten it to merikuri.

items.use: Said in late December when parting from someone you won't see again before New Year.
items.politeJa: よいお年をお迎えください

example.romaji: ja, mata rainen. yoi otoshi o!
example.ja: じゃ、また来年。よいお年を！
example.english: See you next year. Have a good New Year!

examplePolite.romaji: dewa, mata rainen. yoi otoshi o omukae kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: では、また来年。よいお年をお迎えください。
examplePolite.english: See you next year, then. Have a happy New Year.

items.notes: From January 1 on, switch to akemashite omedetou.

items.english: I look forward to another year with you
items.use: New Year greeting said right after akemashite omedetou; answer with the same words, or kochira koso (same here).
items.ja: 今年もよろしくお願いします
items.kana: ことしもよろしくおねがいします

example.romaji: akeome! kotoshi mo yoroshiku ne.
example.ja: あけおめ！今年もよろしくね。
example.english: Happy New Year! Here's to another year.

examplePolite.romaji: kochira koso, kotoshi mo yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: こちらこそ、今年もよろしくお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Same here, I look forward to another year with you.

items.notes: Friends shorten it to kotoshi mo yoroshiku (ne).

items.use: Year-end thanks to coworkers, neighbors, and friends, usually followed by yoi otoshi o.
items.ja: 今年もお世話になりました
items.kana: ことしもおせわになりました

example.romaji: kotoshi mo osewa ni narimashita. mata rainen ne!
example.ja: 今年もお世話になりました。また来年ね！
example.english: Thanks for everything this year. See you next year!

examplePolite.romaji: kotoshi mo osewa ni narimashita. rainen mo yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 今年もお世話になりました。来年もよろしくお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Thank you for everything this year. I look forward to next year.

items.notes: Close friends might just say kotoshi mo arigatou.

blocks.label: Effort and ta-da sounds
blocks.rationale: Fill the moments of lifting, counting in and showing off.
blocks.interference: None.

items.use: Said while lifting something, standing up, or sitting down.

example.romaji: yoisho. kono hako, omoi na.
example.ja: よいしょ。この箱、重いな。
example.english: Oof. This box is heavy.

examplePolite.romaji: yoisho. kono hako, omoi desu ne.
examplePolite.ja: よいしょ。この箱、重いですね。
examplePolite.english: Oof. This box is heavy.

items.notes: Saying it as you sit down is a classic, often joked-about sign of getting older.

items.english: ready, one, two, three!; on three
items.use: Signals everyone to act at once: lifting together, shouting together.

example.romaji: ja, issho ni mochiageyou. seeno!
example.ja: じゃ、一緒に持ち上げよう。せーの！
example.english: OK, let's lift it together. One, two, three!

examplePolite.romaji: ja, issho ni mochiagemashou. seeno!
examplePolite.ja: じゃ、一緒に持ち上げましょう。せーの！
examplePolite.english: OK, let's lift it together. One, two, three!

items.notes: Act on the 'no'; there's no count after it.

items.use: Said while revealing something you're proud of.

example.romaji: jaan! kore, tezukuri no keeki.
example.ja: ジャーン！これ、手作りのケーキ。
example.english: Ta-da! I made this cake myself.

examplePolite.romaji: jaan! kore, tezukuri no keeki desu.
examplePolite.ja: ジャーン！これ、手作りのケーキです。
examplePolite.english: Ta-da! I made this cake myself.

items.notes: jajaan adds more drama.

blocks.label: Ouch and damn it
blocks.rationale: React to pain, defeat and feeling foolish.
blocks.interference: chikushou is rough; yarareta works for anyone.

items.use: Reflex shout at a sudden small pain.

example.romaji: ite! houchou de yubi kitchatta.
example.ja: イテッ！包丁で指切っちゃった。
example.english: Ouch! I cut my finger with the knife.

items.notes: A clipped itai (it hurts); ita! and itai! are the same reflex.

items.english: got me!; they got us; I've been had
items.use: When you're beaten, tricked, or caught out.

example.romaji: yarareta! mata kare ni damasareta.
example.ja: やられた！また彼にだまされた。
example.english: He got me! Fooled by him again.

examplePolite.romaji: yararemashita. mata kare ni damasaremashita.
examplePolite.ja: やられました。また彼にだまされました。
examplePolite.english: He got me. I fell for it again.

items.notes: In action films it also means 'I'm hit'.

items.use: Muttered or shouted in frustration at losing or failing.

example.romaji: chikushou, mata maketa yo.
example.ja: ちくしょう、また負けたよ。
example.english: Damn it, lost again.

items.notes: Literally 'beast'; kuso is even cruder.

items.english: how stupid; I feel so dumb; ridiculous
items.use: Mostly about yourself or a situation, once you realize you wasted your effort.

example.romaji: ichinichi matteta. baka mitai.
example.ja: 一日待ってた。バカみたい。
example.english: I waited all day. I feel so stupid.

examplePolite.romaji: ichinichi matte ita nante, baka mitai desu.
examplePolite.ja: 一日待っていたなんて、バカみたいです。
examplePolite.english: Waiting all day like that, I feel so stupid.

items.notes: Said about another person, it's an insult.

blocks.label: Told you so
blocks.rationale: Point out you were right, or call out a hypocrite.
blocks.interference: yoku iu here is sarcastic, not 'people often say'.

items.use: Said when something turns out just as you predicted.

example.romaji: hora ne, yappari ame futta.
example.ja: ほらね、やっぱり雨降った。
example.english: See? It rained, just like I said.

examplePolite.romaji: hora ne, yappari ame ga furimashita.
examplePolite.ja: ほらね、やっぱり雨が降りました。
examplePolite.english: See? It rained after all.

items.notes: hora alone means 'look' or 'here you go': hora, kore.

items.polite: dakara itta ja nai desu ka
items.use: Said, a bit reproachfully, when someone ignored your warning.
items.ja: だから言ったじゃない
items.kana: だからいったじゃない
items.politeJa: だから言ったじゃないですか

example.romaji: dakara itta ja nai. kasa iru tte.
example.ja: だから言ったじゃない。傘いるって。
example.english: I told you so. I said you'd need an umbrella.

examplePolite.romaji: dakara itta ja nai desu ka. kasa ga iru tte.
examplePolite.ja: だから言ったじゃないですか。傘がいるって。
examplePolite.english: I told you. I said you'd need an umbrella.

items.notes: Men often say dakara itta daro.

items.english: look who's talking; you've got some nerve
items.use: Sarcastic reply when someone says something shameless or hypocritical.

example.romaji: yoku iu yo, jibun mo okureta kuse ni.
example.ja: よく言うよ、自分も遅れたくせに。
example.english: Look who's talking, you were late too.

examplePolite.romaji: yoku iimasu ne. jibun mo okureta no ni.
examplePolite.ja: よく言いますね。自分も遅れたのに。
examplePolite.english: You've got some nerve. You were late too.

items.notes: In a plain statement, yoku iu means 'people often say'.

blocks.label: Hey, stop it
blocks.rationale: Get attention, protest, or hush someone.
blocks.interference: oi is rough; use sumimasen to get a stranger's attention.

items.use: Calls or warns someone sharply; normal between close male friends, rude otherwise.

example.romaji: oi, chotto matte yo.
example.ja: おい、ちょっと待ってよ。
example.english: Hey, wait a sec.

items.notes: To get a stranger's attention say sumimasen instead.

items.english: hey, hey; come on; whoa, whoa
items.use: Mild protest when someone does something careless or over the top.

example.romaji: oioi, sore ore no biiru da yo.
example.ja: おいおい、それ俺のビールだよ。
example.english: Hey, hey, that's my beer.

items.notes: Softer and more joking than a single oi.

items.use: Annoyed outburst at someone's behavior, often from women or kids.

example.romaji: mou! mata okureta no?
example.ja: もうっ！また遅れたの？
example.english: Ugh! You're late again?

items.notes: Same word as mou (already; anymore), but snapped out on its own.

items.use: Hushes someone, often with a finger to the lips.

example.romaji: shii! akachan neteru kara.
example.ja: シーッ！赤ちゃん寝てるから。
example.english: Shh! The baby's sleeping.

examplePolite.romaji: shii! shizuka ni onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: シーッ！静かにお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Shh! Quiet, please.

blocks.label: Leave me alone
blocks.rationale: Recognize the angry outbursts you'll hear in films and fights.
blocks.interference: All are rough except hottoite, the only one safe to say yourself.

items.english: leave me alone; mind your own business
items.use: Pushes someone away when you're upset or don't want their help.
items.politeJa: 放っておいてください

example.romaji: mou hottoite yo. hitori ni shite.
example.ja: もうほっといてよ。一人にして。
example.english: Just leave me alone. Let me be by myself.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, shibaraku houtte oite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、しばらく放っておいてください。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, please leave me be for a while.

items.notes: Short for houtte oite, from houtte oku (leave alone); hottoku is the spoken form.

items.english: how should I know!; who cares!
items.use: Snapped back in anger.

example.romaji: sonna no shiru ka yo!
example.ja: そんなの知るかよ！
example.english: How should I know that!

items.notes: Even plain shiranai can sound cold; wakaranai is the safe 'I don't know'.

items.english: don't mess with me; you've got to be kidding
items.use: Angry outburst at something unfair or insulting; hear it in films, don't use it.

example.romaji: fuzaken na, imasara muri da yo.
example.ja: ふざけんな、今さら無理だよ。
example.english: Are you kidding me? It's way too late now.

items.notes: From fuzakeru (to fool around); fuzakenaide (stop messing around) is milder.

items.use: Angry order to stop something that has gone on too long.
items.politeJa: いい加減にしてください

example.romaji: iikagen ni shiro, nankaime da!
example.ja: いいかげんにしろ、何回目だ！
example.english: Knock it off! How many times is this?

examplePolite.romaji: mou iikagen ni shite kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: もういい加減にしてください。
examplePolite.english: Please, that's enough now.

items.notes: iikagen ni shite is the softer everyday version.

blocks.label: That's how it goes
blocks.rationale: Concede a point or accept how things are.
blocks.interference: All start with sou or sore; sorya sou da is 'obviously', sore wa sou is 'fair point'.

items.use: Agree that something is obvious; sorya is a squeezed sore wa.

example.romaji: sorya sou da yo, juu jikan mo aruita n da kara.
example.ja: そりゃそうだよ、十時間も歩いたんだから。
example.english: Well, of course, we walked for ten hours.

items.notes: Close to sore wa sou, but means 'obviously' more than 'fair point'.

items.use: Accept or explain something you can't change, often as sou iu mon da yo.

example.romaji: shigoto nante, sou iu mon da yo.
example.ja: 仕事なんて、そういうもんだよ。
example.english: That's just how work is.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto wa, sou iu mono desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 仕事は、そういうものですよ。
examplePolite.english: That's just how work is.

items.notes: mon is a casual squeeze of mono (thing).

items.use: Concede a point, often before a but: sore wa sou da kedo...

example.romaji: sore wa sou da kedo, ima wa okane ga nai.
example.ja: それはそうだけど、今はお金がない。
example.english: That's true, but I don't have the money right now.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa sou desu kedo, ima wa okane ga nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: それはそうですけど、今はお金がないんです。
examplePolite.english: That's true, but I don't have the money right now.

items.notes: Online, sore wa sou alone is a stock 'fair point'.

blocks.label: Kidding and asides
blocks.rationale: Mark what you say as a joke, a warning, a secret or a long story.
blocks.interference: None.

items.use: Take back a tease, or a joke someone took seriously.

example.romaji: uso uso, joudan da yo. okotta?
example.ja: うそうそ、冗談だよ。怒った？
example.english: Nah, just kidding. Are you mad?

examplePolite.romaji: joudan desu yo. ki ni shinaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 冗談ですよ。気にしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Just kidding. Don't take it seriously.

items.notes: uso uso (literally 'lie, lie') is another quick 'just kidding'.

items.english: just so you know; let me tell you
items.use: Flags a warning or something you want on record; can sound pushy.

example.romaji: ittoku kedo, watashi wa kankei nai kara ne.
example.ja: 言っとくけど、私は関係ないからね。
example.english: Just so you know, this has nothing to do with me.

items.notes: Short for itte oku kedo; the polite version is itte okimasu ga.

items.english: a lot happened, so...; it's a long story
items.use: Hints at trouble without explaining; listeners usually don't press.

example.romaji: maa, iroiro atte, shigoto yameta n da.
example.ja: まあ、いろいろあって、仕事辞めたんだ。
example.english: Well, a lot happened, and I quit my job.

examplePolite.romaji: maa, iroiro atte, shigoto o yamemashita.
examplePolite.ja: まあ、いろいろあって、仕事を辞めました。
examplePolite.english: Well, it's a long story, but I quit my job.

items.notes: iroiro is 'all sorts'; iroiro arigatou is 'thanks for everything'.

items.english: keep it a secret; it's a secret
items.use: Before or after sharing something private; naisho! alone refuses to tell.

example.romaji: kore, minna ni wa naisho da yo.
example.ja: これ、みんなにはないしょだよ。
example.english: Don't tell anyone about this.

examplePolite.romaji: kore, minna ni wa naisho desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: これ、みんなにはないしょですよ。
examplePolite.english: Please keep this between us.

blocks.label: Steering the conversation
blocks.rationale: Wrap up a plan, pick up a story, or change the topic.
blocks.interference: sou iu koto de wraps things up; sou iu koto ka is 'oh, I see'.

items.english: okay, so that's settled; right, let's go with that
items.use: Wraps up a plan or a call once things are decided, right before saying bye.
items.ja: じゃあ、そういうことで
items.kana: じゃあ、そういうことで

example.romaji: jaa, sou iu koto de. mata ashita ne.
example.ja: じゃあ、そういうことで。また明日ね。
example.english: Okay, that's settled. See you tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: dewa, sou iu koto de yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: では、そういうことでよろしくお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Right, let's go with that, then. Thank you.

items.use: Pick up a story after an interruption.
items.kana: どこまではなしたっけ
items.politeJa: どこまで話しましたっけ

example.romaji: etto, doko made hanashita kke?
example.ja: えっと、どこまで話したっけ？
example.english: Um, where was I?

examplePolite.romaji: etto, doko made hanashimashita kke?
examplePolite.ja: えっと、どこまで話しましたっけ？
examplePolite.english: Um, where was I?

items.notes: kke turns a question into 'what was it again?': namae nan datta kke?

items.english: to change the subject; by the way
items.use: Signals a new topic; tokorode is the textbook 'by the way'.

example.romaji: hanashi kawaru kedo, raishuu no nomikai iku?
example.ja: 話変わるけど、来週の飲み会行く？
example.english: Changing the subject, are you going to next week's drinks?

examplePolite.romaji: hanashi wa kawarimasu ga, raishuu no nomikai ni ikimasu ka?
examplePolite.ja: 話は変わりますが、来週の飲み会に行きますか？
examplePolite.english: To change the subject, are you going to next week's drinks?

blocks.label: Feeling refreshed
blocks.rationale: Say a bath, a drink or a clean-up made you feel better.
blocks.interference: sukkiri is cleared up inside; sappari is clean and fresh.

items.english: that feels better; I feel refreshed; that cleared things up
items.use: After a shower, a good cry, a clean-up or finally getting an answer: anything that clears a heavy or cluttered feeling.

example.romaji: heya katazuketara, sukkiri shita.
example.ja: 部屋片付けたら、すっきりした。
example.english: I tidied my room and feel so much better.

examplePolite.romaji: heya o katazuketara, sukkiri shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 部屋を片付けたら、すっきりしました。
examplePolite.english: I tidied my room and feel much better.

items.notes: sappari is close but leans to feeling physically clean or fresh.

items.english: I feel alive again; that hit the spot
items.use: Said after a cold drink on a hot day, a hot bath or a break; literally 'came back to life'.

example.romaji: aa, tsumetai biiru, ikikaetta!
example.ja: ああ、冷たいビール、生き返った！
example.english: Ah, an ice-cold beer. I feel alive again!

items.notes: In stories it's literal: someone came back to life.

items.use: After a bath, a haircut or a light, clean-tasting meal.

example.romaji: kami kitte, sugoku sappari shita yo.
example.ja: 髪切って、すごくさっぱりしたよ。
example.english: I got a haircut and feel so fresh.

examplePolite.romaji: kami o kitte, sugoku sappari shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 髪を切って、すごくさっぱりしました。
examplePolite.english: I got a haircut and feel really fresh.

items.notes: With a negative it means 'not at all': sappari wakaranai (no idea at all).
